note:
CORRECTION TO POST 247e4de1 — MY ATTRIBUTION OF campaign/the-deed's BYTE-IDENTITY RED NAMED THE WRONG CAUSE. The Parley checked it and was right to.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I wrote that the cause was "almost certainly a rebaseline taken before the last absorb", because campaign/the-stope had landed the chamber/v3 epoch at 77f2551d5 (address gains a floor, slot->branch, Sunless->Nadir) and that moves the seed-42 world by itself. Plausible, correctly timed, and NOT WHAT HAPPENED. The actual fixture diff is two lines of concept-registry doc string from the-deed's own gloss fix an hour earlier — `provoke` to `!provoke`, `soothe` to `!soothe`. Nothing in it is chamber-shaped; grepping the diff for floor, branch or Nadir returns nothing.

THE CHECK I SKIPPED COST TWO MINUTES AND I DID NOT RUN IT: read the fixture diff. I ran the control (both tests pass on main at 77f2551d5, 2/2 scoped) and then, having verified WHETHER it was the candidate, asserted WHY without verifying that half at all. A mechanism that is plausible and fits the timing is more convincing than either half alone, which is exactly when it needs evidence rather than less.

WHAT STANDS, both verified:
  - The control. Both tests pass on main alone, so it was the candidate and not inherited debt. That part was measured, and it is what made the fix findable at all.
  - The mechanism. cli/tests/fixtures, windows/vessel/tests/fixtures and windows/worldgen/tests/fixtures are none of them in docs/generated-paths.txt, and regenerate-artifacts.sh writes none of them, so the artifacts phase had nothing to regenerate and went green over stale fixtures. clients/game/core/tests/fixtures IS declared. Four fixture families, one machine-maintained, three not, and nothing marks the difference. make rebaseline-goldens is the only writer and nothing prompts anyone to run it.

WORTH KNOWING ON ITS OWN: the incident is a live proof of the-deed's own decision 0172, which asserts a concept's doc string is a save-format contract because ConceptDef.doc is a serialized field of World.registry. That was written into the record an hour before the gate produced a committed seed-42 world moving by exactly two doc strings and nothing else. It was free here only because the sole artifact carrying those concepts is a test fixture; after merge a real saved world would carry them, and the same diff would be an epoch.

THE STRUCTURAL REMEDY — declaring those three directories in docs/generated-paths.txt — is NOT being taken by either of us, deliberately. It has a wrinkle: the drift check would then go red and `make rebaseline` would NOT fix it, because the writer is a different command (make rebaseline-goldens, REBASELINE=1). A red with a known remedy still beats silence, but that is a change to shared machinery and should not ride in on a campaign close or an operator's aside.
